AgentQuota.description:
The usage quota one agent program reports on a host, e.g. claude's `5h` and `week` windows.
Each machine is logged in to its own account, so the quota is per host. Sent when anything
but `read_at` changes, and once at host start.

exhausted.description: The program reports it is out of quota.

kind.description: The agent program, e.g. `claude`; a plain string, so a new program needs no schema change.

plan.description: The account's plan, when the program reports it, e.g. `plus`, `Pro`.

read_at.description: When the numbers were read at the source: their staleness, not the scan's.

AgentRole.description:
An agent's declared level and the lead it reports to. Without `level` the agent's role is
removed.

domain.description: What a domain lead owns, e.g. `payments`.

AgentSignal.description:
A structured signal from the agent's own program — a harness hook (`agent-fleet hook
signal` / the statusline wrapper) writes it. `prompt` and `turn_end` open a new episode:
the fold drops the agent's stored signal on them. `detail` carries the program's own
text (an error message, a question) when there is one.

program.description: The agent program, e.g. `claude`; a plain string, so a new program needs no schema change.

AgentState.description: An agent's lifecycle state, as the terminal multiplexer reports it.

AgentStuck.description:
Why an agent on the writer's host is stopped, read off its screen. Sent when the cause
appears or changes; `cause` absent clears the record once the agent works again.

detail.description: What the screen showed, or what was done about it.

until.description: When the condition lifts: a quota window's reset, a rate-limit's retry.

AgentUnmanaged.description:
An agent program running outside every herdr pane tree on `host`, reported by the host's
process scan. `procs: 0`-style clearing: the next scan without it sends the same event minus
`program`.

program.description: The program (`claude`, `devin`, `codex`); absent clears the report.

since.description: When it was first seen unmanaged.

pane.description: Multiplexer pane currently hosting the agent.

AgentUsage.description: What an agent's processes cost: the pane's whole process tree, sampled by its host.

cpu_pct.description: CPU since the previous sample, in percent of one core.

rss_kb.description: Memory, CPU and process count are measured on Linux only; elsewhere just `cwd` is sent.

context.description: A link to the context needed to answer.

owner.description: Who or what has to act: an agent, a resource, an ask.

BlockerResolved.description: Resolves the `blocker.raised` named by the envelope's `re`.

disk_free.description: Bytes available to unprivileged users on the fleet data volume.

HostStats.description:
The host agent's own vitals. Counters run from the host's start, so a drop in `uptime_s`
between two reports is a restart.

cpu_ms.description: User + system CPU time of the host process.

herdr_errors.description: Failed herdr calls and dropped herdr subscriptions.

max_rss_kb.description: Peak resident memory of the host process.

ring_failures.description: Rings that failed or were not followed by `working`.

spooled.description: Events this host sent to the spool instead of the hub.

write_failures.description: Events this host could neither send nor spool.

Level.description: An agent's declared level of responsibility, low to high.

MsgDelivered.description: The `msg.sent` named by `re` reached the agent, which then turned `observed`.

attempts.description: Rings it took, this one included.

rung.description: When the ring that worked was typed.

MsgSent.description: A doorbell: a short prompt pointing at an event or a task.

kind.description: What the recipient should do, e.g. `REVIEW`, `FYI`, `UNBLOCKED`.

ref.description: The event or task the message is about.

QuotaWindow.description: One quota window: `used_pct` of the limit spent, resetting at `resets_at`.

ResourceHold.description:
A process holds (`resource.taken`) or queues for (`resource.waiting`) a resource on its host:
a lock the host reads.

resource.description: The host's name for it, e.g. `sim` or `build.1`.

scope.description: What the process says it is doing.

since.description: When it took the resource or joined the queue.

ResourceLimit.description:
A capacity rule: at most `max` worktrees hold any of `resources` on `host` at once, until
`until`. Replaces the rule of the same `name`; an empty `resources` removes it.

ResourceReleased.description: `pid` let go of the resource or left its queue. Without `pid`: nobody holds or waits for it.

SpawnRequested.description:
`agent-fleet spawn` (or `handoff`) asks the host agent on `host` to create a worktree (or a
workspace in an existing one), start the agent and give it the brief. The requester and the
host may be on different machines.

agent.description: The full id it will have: `agent:<host>/<session>/<name>`.

lead.description: Whom the agent reports to; absent means the requester.

level.description: The `agent.role` level declared once the agent is up.

name.description: The agent's name in its session.

profile.description:
The routing profile that was picked. The host resolves its `kind`, `args`, `unset_env`
and the checkout's `ready` script from its OWN `.agent-fleet/fleet.toml` — a request
never carries executable configuration.

replaces.description: An agent to close once the new one has taken its brief (a handoff).

repo.description: `owner/repo`; the host maps it to a checkout (`host --repo owner/repo=<dir>`).

session.description: The herdr session it runs in.

why.description: Every step of the routing decision, for the views.

worktree.description: An existing checkout: open a workspace there instead of creating a worktree.

SpawnResult.description: The `spawn.requested` named by `re`, answered by the host that ran it.

pane.description: The pane the agent runs in.

worktree.description: The worktree or checkout the agent works in.

StuckCause.description: Why an agent is stuck, as its host reads it off the screen.

oneOf.description: The program's account is out of quota.
A short rate-limit wait: `until` is when to retry.
A prompt sits in the input box, never sent.
The program's context is nearly full.
An error on screen waits on a nudge or a human.
A permission or trust prompt (herdr reports `blocked`, or the program signaled one).
The program is asking the operator something.
The program reports an account problem (billing, hold, auth).
Its worktree holds or waits on a resource; a legitimate wait, not a hang.
Its task is deliberately held: an open blocker or an unfinished dep.
Idle after working, nothing blocking on screen.
None of the above matched.

url.description: Where the spec lives (an issue, a doc).

TaskState.description: Task lifecycle, aligned with the A2A task states.

WorktreeProcs.description:
Processes running in a worktree that no agent's process tree holds: dev servers, databases,
test runs, shells. Sent each scan while there are any, then once with `procs: 0`.

orphaned.description: The directory is gone: nothing that could stop these processes knows they are there.

WorktreeState.description: A git worktree on a host, as its last scan found it. Sent when it changes.

files.description: Files changed against the default branch, plus dirty ones; at most `MAX_FILES`.

in_main.description:
Everything this branch changed is already in the default branch (merged, squashed or
never started): it holds no work of its own.

repo.description: The main checkout the worktree belongs to.

unpushed.description: Commits on HEAD that no remote has.

event.description: Every event: the envelope fields plus a `type` tag and its `data`.

id.description: ULID chosen by the writer. Appending the same id twice is a no-op.

re.description: The event this one answers or follows.

v.description: Schema version of this event's type.

event.title: Event

worked.description: When it was last seen `working`; a stall is an idle stretch after this.

AgentState.description: An agent's lifecycle state, as the terminal multiplexer reports it.

Level.description: An agent's declared level of responsibility, low to high.

Quota.description: A program's usage quota on one host, as its last `agent.quota` reported it.

exhausted_since.description:
When the reports first showed the account out; kept while it stays out, absent
while it does not.

read_at.description: When the numbers were read at the source: how stale they are.

ts.description: When the report was folded in.

QuotaWindow.description: One quota window: `used_pct` of the limit spent, resetting at `resets_at`.

ResourceLimit.description:
A capacity rule: at most `max` worktrees hold any of `resources` on `host` at once, until
`until`. Replaces the rule of the same `name`; an empty `resources` removes it.

Role.description:
An agent's declared level and the lead it reports to; `by` and `since` record the
`agent.role` event that set it.

Spawn.description:
A `spawn.requested` and the `spawn.result` that answered it. `by` and `project` come from the
request's envelope.

answered.description: The answering event's `ts`; finished spawns are pruned 24 h after it.

worktree.description: The worktree or checkout the agent works in.

Stuck.description: An agent's current stuck record: the latest `agent.stuck` with a cause.

until.description: When the condition lifts, if the cause names one.

TaskState.description: Task lifecycle, aligned with the A2A task states.

Unmanaged.description: An agent program the host's scan saw outside every herdr pane tree.

WorktreeProcs.description:
Processes running in a worktree that no agent's process tree holds: dev servers, databases,
test runs, shells. Sent each scan while there are any, then once with `procs: 0`.

orphaned.description: The directory is gone: nothing that could stop these processes knows they are there.

WorktreeState.description: A git worktree on a host, as its last scan found it. Sent when it changes.

files.description: Files changed against the default branch, plus dirty ones; at most `MAX_FILES`.

in_main.description:
Everything this branch changed is already in the default branch (merged, squashed or

repo.description: The main checkout the worktree belongs to.

unpushed.description: Commits on HEAD that no remote has.

asks.description: Open asks by the id of their `ask.raised`.

blockers.description: Open blockers by the id of their `blocker.raised`.

last.description: Id of the last event folded in.

msgs.description: Undelivered doorbells by the id of their `msg.sent`.

quotas.description: Usage quotas of the agent programs by `<host>:<kind>`.

refused_kills.description: The latest kills `agent-fleet kill` refused, oldest first; at most `MAX_REFUSED`.

roles.description: Declared roles by agent id; kept apart from `agents`, so a role survives `agent.down`.

signals.description:
The latest `agent.signal` per agent, keyed by agent id; cleared when a `prompt` or
`turn_end` signal opens a new episode, and when the agent turns `working` or goes down.

spawns.description: Spawn requests by their `spawn.requested` id; answered ones are kept for 24 h.

stuck.description: Why a stopped agent is stopped, as its host read it off the screen, keyed by agent id.

unknown.description:
Events this binary cannot fold (an unknown type, or a known type at a newer `v`): kept in
the log, skipped here.

unmanaged.description: Agent programs outside herdr on each host, keyed `<host>:<pid>`.

worktree_procs.description: Processes running in worktrees (or orphaned beside them) by `<host>:<path>`.
